findings.title: [P1] Preserve database-equivalent ID matches when rebuilding results
findings.body: The new reconstruction joins DB rows back to requests with exact string equality: `byId.get(id) ?? null` against a `Map` keyed by `row.id`. Databases do not always return IDs byte-identical to the input: PostgreSQL normalizes UUID text to lowercase (while accepting uppercase input), and MySQL/SQL Server case-insensitive collations match `'ABC'` to stored `'abc'`. In those setups — common in TypeScript server codebases — `findMany` retrieves the row, but `byId.get('ABC')` misses and `loadUsers` silently returns `null` for a user that exists. The previous `db.users.find(id)` per-ID lookup returned that row, so this is a behavior regression under realistic inputs, and it fails silently rather than erroring. Matching rows back should tolerate the database's normalization (e.g. key the map the same way the database compares, or fall back per unresolved ID), or the ID form should be normalized on both sides.
